questions.stem: Telemetry from 30,000 vending machines arrives as a stream of events, and support engineers run interactive, fine-grained queries over the last hours. Which store fits?

options.text: A warehouse, loaded each night with COPY INTO from the event files
A SQL database in Fabric, with one row inserted for every event as it arrives
An eventhouse, queried with KQL
A lakehouse, read through its SQL analytics endpoint by the support engineers

questions.explanation: The decision guide says: for streaming event data and high-granularity interactive analytics, use an eventhouse. Its primary languages are KQL and T-SQL.

questions.stem: An order-entry app needs an operational, normalized relational database for many small reads and writes. Which store fits?

options.text: An eventhouse, with each order sent in as an event
A warehouse, with the app writing through its T-SQL endpoint
A lakehouse, with each order saved as a small Delta file
A SQL database in Fabric

questions.explanation: For operational, transactional, OLTP workloads or normalized relational databases, the guide says to use SQL database in Fabric.

questions.stem: The finance team writes T-SQL, builds a star schema, and its loads must update several tables in one transaction. Which store fits?

options.text: An eventhouse, with each table loaded by its own update policy
A warehouse
A lakehouse, loaded by a T-SQL script run against its SQL analytics endpoint
A lakehouse, with a Spark notebook writing each table on its own

questions.explanation: For T-SQL, the lakehouse or warehouse guide says to use a warehouse. If you need multi-table transactions, use a warehouse: it has full DQL, DML and DDL T-SQL with full transaction support.

questions.stem: Data scientists work in PySpark over images, JSON and CSV files, and they train models on them. Which store fits?

options.text: An eventhouse, with the files sent in as events
A SQL database in Fabric, with each file stored in a varbinary column
A warehouse, with the files loaded into wide varchar columns
A lakehouse

questions.explanation: For big data and machine learning with unstructured, semi-structured or structured data, and for data engineering, the guide says to use a lakehouse. Its primary languages are Spark (Scala, PySpark, Spark SQL, R).

questions.stem: A team will query a lakehouse through its SQL analytics endpoint. Which two can they do there with T-SQL?

options.text: Run INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE statements on the Delta tables
Run SELECT queries over the lakehouse's Delta tables
Create SQL views over those tables
Run COPY INTO to load new files into the lakehouse's tables

questions.explanation: The SQL analytics endpoint is read-only for data: full DQL, no DML, and limited DDL such as SQL views and table-valued functions. Loading with COPY INTO or INSERT needs a warehouse.
